If we don't have this for our testnets, if an EL/CL pair goes out-of-sync then those CL nodes are most likely going to start producing attestations for old heads. This generally means lots of skip slots, heavy resource usage and general network chaos. <terencechain> Good point for testnets, but this is not the intended behavior for mainnet right? Im under the impression if EL node is syncing / not reachable then CL node will just pack in ExecutionPayload() (re @sigpaul: After @ethzed pointed it out to me, I've added a constraint to our BN HTTP API that we won't serve any requests for duties or publish any consensus messages after the merge-fork-epoch if we don't have a synced and reachable execution engine. This generally means lots of skip slots, heavy resource usage and general network chaos.

If empty, it is waiting to transition

excerpts.author: bridge-bot
excerpts.content:
<sigpaul> > the eth1 config defines the genesis execution payload
but that definition is not provided by the spec, right?

excerpts.author: bridge-bot
excerpts.content: <dannyryan> It is network specific

excerpts.author: bridge-bot
excerpts.content:
<dannyryan> The hardcoded, e.g., initial gas limit was incorrect in v1.1.0
As it should be defined based on the actual eth1/el genesis block

excerpts.author: bridge-bot
excerpts.content: <sigpaul> Got it, thanks. BYO, you-do-you ExecutionPayloadHeader.

excerpts.author: bridge-bot
excerpts.content:
<sigpaul> And this quirk still exists, right? (re @sigpaul: Hmm, it seems that the spec is a little unclear here.
On the one hand, the genesis block should have an all-zeros execution payload since we define the genesis block as:
genesis_block = BeaconBlock(state_root=hash_tree_root(genesis_state))
On the other hand, the BeaconState has the latest_execution_payload_header set to some initial values.
Since LH is loading the genesis block from the DB to obtain the latest block hash, it's returning all-zeros. However, if it loaded the BeaconState and read the latest header it'd get a different value.
I'm really starting to feel that the merge initialize_beacon_state_from_eth1 is a waste of time and we should just do the fork transition. There's less edge-cases and we get to test the fork more.)

excerpts.author: bridge-bot
excerpts.content:
<dannyryan> Im not sure I understand the quirk
The genesis state should have the init latest exec payload header embedded in it
And the genesis beacon block should reference such a state

excerpts.author: bridge-bot
excerpts.content: <sigpaul> But the genesis block has a different execution_payload to the state's latest_execution_payload_header.

excerpts.author: bridge-bot
excerpts.content: <dannyryan> I see

excerpts.author: bridge-bot
excerpts.content: <dannyryan> This is probably correct behaviour as the genesis block is not applied as a transition to anything, nor does it end up embedded in state (avoiding a circular ref)

excerpts.author: bridge-bot
excerpts.content: <dannyryan> I'll think about it when get to computer now that I know the actual issue referenced!

excerpts.author: bridge-bot
excerpts.content:
<sigpaul> cool!
It would be a shame that we can't say "the block.body.execution_payload.block_hash always corresponds to the corresponding execution block hash".
It becomes an issue in implementation because you can't just read the (small) block from the DB, you need the (big) state. It wouldn't be too hard to work around it, since it's a rare special-case. But we all know what happens with "rare special-cases" in implementations 😬

excerpts.author: bridge-bot
excerpts.content: <dannyryan> Yeah I see that. And no circular reference or anything
